post.instagram_caption:
The computer that guided Apollo 11 to the Moon had about 4 KB of working memory.

NASA's history of the Apollo Guidance Computer lists 2,048 words of erasable memory and 36,864 words of fixed memory, a clock of about one megahertz, and a weight of 70.1 pounds. The fixed memory was core rope: wires sewn together by women in factories (CBS News).

For scale: a phone with 8 GB of RAM has about 2 million times more working memory.

The lesson: it is not how much computer you have, it is how well you use it.

Source: NASA, "Computers in Spaceflight: The NASA Experience"; CBS News.

post.youtube_description:
The Apollo Guidance Computer that took Apollo 11 to the Moon had 2,048 words of erasable memory (about 4 KB) and 36,864 words of fixed memory, ran at about one megahertz and weighed 70.1 pounds, according to NASA. Its fixed memory was core rope, wires sewn together by hand in factories. A phone with 8 GB of RAM has about 2 million times more working memory.

Sources:
• NASA, "Computers in Spaceflight: The NASA Experience", Chapter 2
• CBS News Boston, "Apollo 11's 4th Crew Member: A Ground-Breaking, 70 Pound Computer" (Jun 28, 2019)
• Ken Shirriff, "Inside the Apollo Guidance Computer's core memory" (2019)
